html:
The Kariyarra are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Pilbara coast of Western Australia, around present-day Port Hedland. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815. Their language forms a dialect chain with that of the Ngarluma to the west, and speakers of the two can understand each other.

Other neighbours were the Yindjibarndi inland, the Ngarla to the east and the Nyamal to the southeast. Sheep stations spread over their land from the 1860s. Port Hedland grew in the 20th century into one of the world's biggest ports for shipping iron ore.
